contentBlocks.title: Pending for 30+ Days — What to Do
contentBlocks.description: Your SASSA grant has been pending for more than 30 days — this is longer than usual. Find out why your application may be stuck, what you can do to speed things up, and when to escalate to a SASSA office.

contentBlocks.text: Pending for 30+ Days — What It Means

If your SASSA grant status has been 'Pending' for more than 30 days, it indicates a delay in the verification process. While the standard processing time is 7 to 14 business days for SRD and up to 3 months for other grants, extended pending periods can signal a bottleneck that needs your attention.
This status affects SASSA grant applicants whose applications have been in the review process for more than 30 days without a final decision.

contentBlocks.title: Longer Than 8 Weeks?
contentBlocks.text: If your status has been pending for more than 8 weeks, visit your nearest SASSA office to follow up. There may be a documentation issue.

contentBlocks.explanation: Your application has been in the verification queue longer than expected. This typically means automated checks could not be completed and your file requires manual review by a SASSA officer.
whyItHappens: High volume of applications causing processing backlog
Delays in receiving database confirmation from UIF or Home Affairs
Mismatched contact or bank details requiring manual verification
Your application was flagged for additional document verification
contentBlocks.howLongItLasts: Variable. It remains pending until a SASSA officer manually reviews your file or the system completes the pending checks. If unresolved after 45 days, escalate.
whatYouShouldDo: Log into the SRD portal to check for outstanding document requests
Verify your bank details are correct and your account is active
If 45 days pass without progress, contact the SASSA toll-free helpline at 0800 60 10 11
Visit your nearest SASSA office if the helpline cannot resolve the issue
whatToCheck: Log into the SRD portal to check if there is an unread alert or document request banner.
Verify with your bank that your account has not been closed, dormant, or restricted under FICA.
Check the Department of Labour uFiling portal to ensure an old employer did not register an active contract.

contentBlocks.text: Illustrative example: day 38 with no movement

Sipho applied on 2 October. By 9 November — 38 days later — his status had not moved beyond Pending. Instead of calling immediately, he worked through the three databases that usually cause the hold-up: the SRD portal for any unread document request, his bank for a dormant or FICA-restricted account, and uFiling for an employment record that was opened and never closed.

The last check found the problem. A former employer had registered him for a contract that ended in August but never filed the termination. He requested a UI-19 termination certificate, then visited his nearest SASSA office with that letter and his ID so the record could be annotated. That is the point at which a phone call or an office visit becomes worth the queue: once there is a specific, documented discrepancy to correct.

steps.title: Check for an outstanding request
steps.description: Open the SRD portal and look for a banner or prompt asking for a document or a selfie.

steps.title: Check your bank account is usable
steps.description: A dormant, closed or FICA-restricted account blocks payment even when eligibility has passed.

steps.title: Check for an open UIF record
steps.description: An unclosed employment record is the most common invisible cause of a long Pending.

steps.title: Escalate with evidence
steps.description: After 45 days, take the specific document that shows the discrepancy to SASSA rather than describing it from memory.

contentBlocks.text: The toll-free SASSA helpline is 0800 60 10 11, and a district office can annotate a record that the automated checks cannot clear. Employment records are held by the Department of Employment and Labour and can be viewed on uFiling, which is where a UI-19 letter or termination certificate originates. Neither SASSA nor the department publishes a guaranteed resolution time for a manual correction, which is why this page describes the evidence to bring rather than a deadline to expect.

faqs.question: Will I get backpay if my application is pending for months?
faqs.answer: Yes. Once approved, SASSA backdates payment to the month you first applied. You will receive a lump sum for all months that were pending.

faqs.question: Can I speed up a pending application?
faqs.answer: No, but you can ensure no action is needed from your side by logging into the portal and checking for outstanding requests.

faqs.question: Should I submit a new application while the old one is pending?
faqs.answer: No. Submitting a duplicate application will cause further delays and may result in a 'Duplicate Application' decline.
